subject: Mutual plan: evaluation success lattice, exit signals, and acceptance test playbook
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novamed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Defining success: NovaMed evaluation — what we need from Redwood

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We've carved out a four-week evaluation window to validate Redwood with a representative workload (see attached high-level requirements). Before we kick off we'd like a concise mutual action plan (MAP) that defines:

- Success criteria (quantitative thresholds we can measure)
- Exit gates (hard fail conditions that stop the eval)
- Acceptance tests (how we'll validate each criterion)
- Timeline and owner assignments for each test

Key priorities for us: latency p95 under 450ms for 99% of calls, end-to-end inference cost per 1k tokens target, feature parity on structured output for our triage workflow, and proof that data never leaves our VPC during the pilot.

Can you send a MAP draft and acceptance test matrix we can review by EOD Wednesday? Procurement will need a projected signature date if the pilot looks good — they want to align legal and SOC2 evidence requests up front. CC'd Ben from your side for the technical fit.

Attachments: NovaMed_requirements_v1.xlsx (workload profile, sample prompts, compliance checklist)

Best,
Elaine Park
Director of AI Engineering
NovaMed Health

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Defining success: NovaMed evaluation — what we need from Redwood

Elaine — thank you, this is super clear. Attaching a first-pass MAP and an acceptance_test_matrix (CSV) with measurable checks. High level summary below, plus proposed owners and timeline so procurement and engineering can slot tasks.

Quick summary (MAP v0.1):
- Trial window: 4 weeks (pilot start Tue May 18 — end Tue Jun 15).
- Primary success signals:
  * Latency: p95 < 450ms for 99% of non-batched requests (measured at Redwood edge to NovaMed app).
  * Functional correctness: structured JSON outputs match ground-truth schema with >= 92% key-level accuracy across 200 sample prompts.
  * Stability: 99.5% success rate (no runtime exceptions) across projected throughput profile.
  * Data residency: all inference traffic remains inside NovaMed VPC via Private deployment or VPC peering; log access limited to named custodians.
  * Cost guardrail: projected inference cost per 1k tokens within 15% of the estimate in NovaMed_requirements_v1.xlsx.
- Exit gates (hard stop — evaluation terminates if any occur):
  * Model responses that expose PHI or PII in >0.1% of random sample checks.
  * Failure rate >1.5% for more than 6 hours consecutive.
  * Reproducible data exfil evidence (logs show outbound IPs outside agreed VPC ranges).
- Acceptance tests (examples in attached CSV):
  * Latency sweep: 3x runs at low/medium/high concurrency, p95 computation and traces. Owner: Ben Carter.
  * Schema conformance: run 200 labeled prompts through the pipeline, compute key-level precision/recall. Owner: Marissa Cole.
  * Fault injection: simulated node restarts + KV cache clears to validate cold start SLAs. Owner: Ben Carter.
  * Privacy audit: validate network flow logs and storage permissions; provide signed attestation. Owner: Redwood Security Team (we will coordinate SOC2 artifacts).

Proposed timeline and owners:
- Wed May 12: Redwood shares MAP v0.1 (attached) and acceptance_test_matrix.csv (today).
- Tue May 18: Pilot kickoff; infra provisioning completed by Redwood; sample dataset ingestion begins. Owner: Ben.
- Week 1 (May 18–24): Latency/stability baseline and quick functional smoke tests.
- Week 2 (May 25–31): Full acceptance test run (schema conformance, cost sampling).
- Week 3 (Jun 1–7): Edge/scale tests, fault injection.
- Week 4 (Jun 8–15): Final pass, remediation, mutual review; decision by Jun 18.

Next steps: Elaine — can you confirm the kickoff date (May 18) and the internal stakeholders who will validate the schema conformance results? Procurement contact as well so we can provide an estimated SOW and timeline for signature.

Attachments: RDW_MAP_draft_v1.xlsx, acceptance_test_matrix.csv

Thanks — Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novamed.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Defining success: NovaMed evaluation — what we need from Redwood

Adding a few technical specifics and proposed test scripts (high level) so owners have explicit acceptance criteria. I dropped these into acceptance_test_matrix.csv (rows we will automate):

1) Latency sweep (script: latency_sweep.sh)
   - Inputs: 3 concurrency profiles (10/100/500 qps mimic).
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tail latency spikes, CPU/GPU utilization.
   - Pass: p95 < 450ms for 99% of the runs.

2) Functional conformance (script: schema_check.py)
   - Inputs: 200 labeled prompts (with canonical JSON outputs).
   - Metrics: key-level accuracy, empty-field rate, hallucination rate via fuzzy-match.
   - Pass: >=92% key-level accuracy and hallucination <5% for critical fields.

3) Cold-start resilience (script: crash_recovery.jsonl runner)
   - Test: drain and restart 1 of 3 serving nodes mid-run; ensure total error rate spike <1% and recovery <5 minutes.

4) KV cache correctness
   - Test: run long conversation sequences to ensure cache produces deterministic continuation tokens and does not leak context between sessions.

5) Privacy/network runbook
   - Checklist: VPC endpoints verified, no public egress, signed ACL snapshot.

Notes for timing: most of these are scriptable and can be executed during Week 2/3. I recommend we automate the CSV import to NovaMed's test harness so we produce a reproducible report.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novamed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@novamed.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Defining success: NovaMed evaluation — what we need from Redwood

Grace/Ben — this looks good and granular enough for our teams to operationalize. A couple of small adjustments from our side:

- Functional suite: add a small set of adversarial prompts (25) that target hallucination modes — we'll provide them by Fri May 14.
- Latency tolerance: we can accept p95 up to 500ms for burst windows if it’s clearly signaled and transient (documented in the report).
- Procurement: we need an estimated signature date. Can Redwood commit to providing a draft SOW and pricing target by May 20? If yes, I'll put a note on our side to expedite legal review.

We agree to the hard exit gates (PHI leakage, sustained failure rate, reproducible egress). I'll loop in Carlos (engineering lead) and Procurement on the kickoff once we lock the May 18 date.

Thanks — Elaine

Subject: Re: Defining success: NovaMed evaluation — what we need from Redwood

Elaine/Carlos/Team — kickoff confirmed for today. Infra provisioning completed early this morning (we've attached provisioning logs to the shared Drive). A few operational notes and the finalized MAP v0.2:

- Pilot start: May 18 (today). Sample ingestion in progress; expected time to first functional smoke tests = 6 hours.
- Acceptance artifacts: acceptance_test_matrix.csv now includes the adversarial prompts column and explicit pass/fail script commands.
- Procurement: Grace (me) will share a draft SOW and pricing range by Thu May 20; Ben will include estimated infra delta for Dedicated vs Private. Link: https://drive.google.com/novamed/RDW_MAP_draft_v1
- DocuSign: I uploaded the preliminary commercial term sheet to DocuSign for visibility; Procurement can ignore until after the evaluation.

Immediate ask for NovaMed: please confirm the list of schema owners who will validate the functional conformance outputs (names + emails) so Marissa can schedule the automated run.

We'll run the Week 1 smoke tests and share a reproducible report by May 21. If any hard exit gate trips we will pause the pilot and notify stakeholders with root cause and mitigation plan.

Thanks everyone — excited to get started.

Grace O'Connor
Sr. Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
